What was built:
- A new 'mem-block' scene, labelled "Memory block" in the Structure control, added to the scene map in both directions (URL sync works).
- MemBlockScene.tsx holds the scene. It has pure layout helpers (memLanes, laneBits, drawerBits, memReadSet, lanesRead, memBlockSummary, cubeX/drawerY), each exported and tested. It contains no select rules: value, kind, type, bit arithmetic, steps, notes, the question and the prediction options all come from sv-array-select-model.ts (evaluateCase, selectQuestion, selectOptions, orderedOptions). That model is imported only, never edited.
- The chips come from the model: mem[5], mem[5][2] and mem[5][2][3] are the model's own SELECT_CASES. mem[16] takes its index from the declaration bound (bound + 1), and mem[i] is built with i = 'x.
- The 3D view draws 16 drawers, each a gapless row of 32 instanced bit cubes. A 1 is a tall cube in cyan, a 0 a flat tile in slate, and x is rose, so value is shown by shape as well as colour. The byte value from the model's formatBits is written on each lane, and mem[i] labels mark the drawers.
- After the reveal, unselected cubes dim and the selection gets a solid outline plus an "expr = value" label. An invalid index shows a dashed ghost drawer: after the last drawer for mem[16], floating above the block for i = 'x, since an x index has no position. Its bits come from the model: 'x for logic, '0 for bit.
- The canvas uses frameloop="demand" and calls invalidate after instance updates. OrbitCont

findings: Verified against IEEE 1800-2023 §7.4.5 and Table 7-1 (t1_lrm_clean.txt, around offset 485800). The source says an index is invalid if it is out of bounds or if any of its bits is x or z. A read through an invalid index into an unpacked array returns the Table 7-1 value: 'x for a 4-state integral type, '0 for a 2-state one, and for a fixed-size unpacked array, an array whose every element has that value. A write through an invalid index does nothing, except for queue [$+1] and a new associative-array element. Implementations may issue a warning. The model branch in src/lib/sv-array-select-model.ts (around lines 268-300) matches all of this. It gives the reasons out-of-bounds and x-index, the step 'Writing through an invalid index does nothing (§7.4.5)', and the note 'Implementations may issue a warning for an invalid index (§7.4.5)'. MemBlockScene adds no rules of its own: it renders result.steps and result.notes (around lines 485-489).

Checked against IEEE 1800-2023. §7.4.4 (joe example) says 'When referenced, the packed dimensions ... follow the unpacked dimensions' and 'the rightmost one varies most rapidly'. It also says subarrays are referenced by omitting indices, always omitting the ones that vary most rapidly. §7.4.1 says a packed array is a contiguous set of bits, an unpacked array may or may not be, and a packed primary is a single vector. §11.5.1 says the bit an address reaches is 'in part, determined by the declaration'. §7.4.5 says slices apply to one dimension and an invalid index into an unpacked array returns the Table 7-1 value. The cited clause numbers are all real and correctly attributed.

Checked the distractors by working out the wrong paths by hand. from-left for mem[5][2] gives 8'h51 (lane [1]). from-left for mem[5][2][3] gives bit 11. swapped mem[5][3][2] gives bit 26, which is 1'b0 because 0x53 bit 2 = 0. swapped mem[2][5] gives 8'hxx because [5] is outside [3:0] (§11.5.1 via §7.4.5). All are correct for the misreading they name.

I ran the model: 'sh8000_0000, 'shFFFF_FFFF, 'sd4294967295 and 'sd2147483648 each get minWidth=33 and the text 'its value needs more, so it has at least 33 bits, sign bit included.
